name: initiative_under_goal
description: Two leaves share the SAME top-level goal; only an initiative in between differs in importance. A formula that reads only the top-level ancestor, ignoring everything between it and the leaf, sees the identical root for both and cannot produce the stated order.

nodes.label: Strategic goal both leaves sit under
Initiative under the shared goal, deprioritized after a reorg
Initiative under the same shared goal, still important

notes: Both leaves sit under the identical top-level goal (goal_shared, 0.9); only the intermediate initiative differs (0.95 vs 0.1). The leaves' OWN importance is deliberately NOT equal here (0.5 vs 0.6) -- a small, controlled asymmetry needed to turn two formerly-degenerate ties into formulas that actually disagree, rather than a true isolation of the initiative alone (that's what 05_deprioritized_initiative already covers). task_under_important_initiative=0.5, task_under_deprioritized_initiative=0.6, initiative_still_important=0.95 (now above the root's 0.9), initiative_deprioritized=0.1, goal_shared=0.9. Worked arithmetic for all five formulas: additive-boost (own+sum(ancestors)): important = 0.5+0.95+0.9=2.35, deprioritized = 0.6+0.1+0.9=1.6 -- important wins by 0.75, correct order, no tie. multiplicative (own*ancestor1*ancestor2): important = 0.5*0.95*0.9=0.4275, deprioritized = 0.6*0.1*0.9=0.054 -- important wins by a wide margin, correct order. average-of-own-plus-all-ancestors-inclusive: important = (0.5+0.95+0.9)/3=0.783, deprioritized = (0.6+0.1+0.9)/3=0.533 -- important wins, correct order. All three preserve the stated order because the initiative gap (0.95-0.1=0.85) dwarfs the own-importance gap (0.6-0.5=0.1) we introduced. root-only (own+root alone, blind to the initiative): important = 0.5+0.9=1.4, deprioritized = 0.6+0.9=1.5 -- deprioritized now scores HIGHER, a genuinely wrong order (not a tie), because both leaves get the same root contribution and the own-importance asymmetry we added tips it the wrong way. own+max(ancestors): important = 0.5+max(0.95,0.9)=0.5+0.95=1.45, deprioritized = 0.6+max(0.1,0.9)=0.6+0.9=1.5 -- deprioritized again scores higher, a wrong order, not a tie: making initiative_still_important (0.95) exceed the root (0.9) breaks the structural guarantee that max always resolves to the shared root for both leaves, and the 0.1 own-importance asymmetry (which exceeds the 0.05 margin by which initiative_still_important clears the root) is enough to flip the comparison. So root-only and own+max(ancestors) -- the two formulas this fixture targets -- now fail deterministically and distinguishably, while the three formulas already treated as robust elsewhere in this suite still pass with comfortable margins.
